newsitem.title: UK: Brown gives UK health service, education more cash.
newsitem.headline: Brown gives UK health service, education more cash.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said he was allocating extra funds to the National Health Service and education in fiscal 1998-99 from the contingency reserve.
"I have decided to allocate from the reserve to the NHS for 1998-99 a sum of 1.2 billion stg," he said.
This means that health spending will now rise by five percent, 2.25 percent in real terms, he said.
He also announced that education would be allocated one billion stg next year from the reserves.

"In normal circumstances, the five billion stg reserve for 1998-99 -- set aside by the previous government -- would be distributed during the annual Autumn spending round - with allocation announced at the time of the November budget," he said.
But there is no spending round this Autumn, he said.
Brown also said that some of the proceeds of the windfall tax on privatised utilities would be allocated to capital investment in schools.
"I therefore propose to make available 1.3 billion stg over the course of the parliament, representing a capital investment that averages almost 150 stg for every pupil in the country," he said.
The new resources total 2.3 billion stg for schools, Brown said. --Cheryl Juckes +44 171 542 5109
